assumptions: Under the null the gene is exchangeable with every other gene the tables score.
The tables are fixed before the gene's scores are seen.
limits: The product of e-values is valid only when the tests are independent under the null; the joint p is the answer whatever their dependence.
Two or three tables answer fewer questions than a program of tests designed for the hypothesis.
bio.jane/contract.question: Does the evidence in a set of gene-level tables support a hypothesis that one gene drives a phenotype, by sequential falsification?

description: Test a hypothesis that a gene drives a phenotype ("gene G regulates IL-2 production") the way POPPER does: each evidence table is one falsification test, an implication of the hypothesis that a gene-level score could contradict (expression in the relevant tissue, association with related disease, interaction with genes annotated to the process). Under the null that G is exchangeable with any gene the tables score, G's p in each table is the share of genes scoring at or beyond it; each p is calibrated to the e-value κ·p^(κ−1), the e-values are multiplied in the order given, and the hypothesis passes when the product exceeds 1/α. The product is a valid e-value only when the tests are independent under the null, so the run also reports the joint p: the product's own share among every gene's product, valid whatever the tables' dependence. Returns every test's score, rank, p, e and running product, the test after which the product first crossed 1/α, and the joint p. Each table is `gene<TAB>score` with one header line; the gene must be in every table.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alpha.description: the hypothesis passes when the product of e-values exceeds 1/α.

gene.description: the gene under test, as the tables spell it (HGNC symbol for the bundled corpus).

kappa.description: κ of the p-to-e calibrator κ·p^(κ−1); POPPER's default is 0.5. Advanced.

tables.description: the falsification tests in the order to apply them: each `{ name, text, direction }`, where `text` is `gene<TAB>score` with a header line and `direction` is the end of the score the hypothesis predicts, `greater` (default) or `less`.

name: discover_target_validation

combined.description: the product of the calibrated e-values

jointP.description: the product's share among every gene's product

nullModel.description: the null, stated with every run

rejected.description: whether the product of e-values exceeded 1/α

tests.description: each test: score, genes at or beyond, p, e and running product
